claims.text: Conventionally processed Ta20Nb20Hf20Zr20Ti20-based refractory HEAs have a continuous brittle B2 matrix.
A processing route combining hot isostatic pressing, controlled rolling, and annealing near 900°C can produce an inverted microstructure in Ta20Nb20Hf20Zr20Ti20-based refractory HEAs.
The resulting inverted microstructure consists of a continuous ductile BCC matrix containing finely dispersed, isolated B2 precipitates.
Discrete B2 precipitates impede dislocation motion.
Impeded dislocation motion caused by the B2 precipitates increases yield strength.
A continuous BCC matrix preserves ductility.
The proposed inverted microstructure will improve high-temperature yield strength by approximately 15–25% relative to conventionally processed material.
The proposed inverted microstructure will enhance ductility by approximately 15–25% relative to conventionally processed material.
The predicted mechanical-property improvements can be sustained at service temperatures up to 1023 K if the inverted microstructure remains stable.
Long-term effectiveness depends on preventing degradation of the B2 precipitate distribution and BCC matrix during prolonged high-temperature exposure.
Performance beyond 1023 K or under significantly different loading conditions is uncertain.
Precipitate coarsening or matrix reversion during aging would constitute degradation of the proposed inverted microstructure.
